summary:
[  edit  ]
The MIDI Out  CHOP  sends  MIDI  events to any available MIDI devices when its input channels change. More flexibly, the Python  midioutCHOP Class  can be used to send any type of MIDI event to a MIDI device via an existing MIDI Out  CHOP . In  Tscript , the  midi  command can output MIDI events.
The MIDI devices can be other software programs (such as midisynth) or devices attached to the serial ports. Channels are used to control the sending of the MIDI events. The channels are evaluated over the last time slice (from the last  Timeline  position to the current).
The MIDI Out  CHOP  sends MIDI events based on any changes to its input channels. The channels have to be named appropriately, like  ch3c14  and  ch7n60 .
An event is sent every time a channel changes its value during this slice. All timing is preserved, as long as the  Timeline  is running in realtime (the "Realtime" flag is in the top menu bar).
Naming the  CHOP  channels: Channels are mapped to events by their name. Events like notes, controllers and velocities must be followed by the note/controller number (n65, c7). If the number is left off a note event, the note number is the value of the channel. Other events, which are sent to the entire channel, do not need a trailing number (pc, pw). The channel prefix can be used to identify the MIDI channel the event should be sent on (i.e. "ch1n45" assigns that TouchDesigner channel to note 45 messages on MIDI channel 1).  Channels can always be renamed with a  Rename CHOP  before entering the  MIDI Out CHOP .
The MIDI Out  CHOP  sends MIDI velocity as well. The values of the channels entering the MIDI Out CHOPs are sent as the velocity of the note. If Normalize is "None", the channel needs to be 0 to 127. If Normalize is "0 to 1", channel values between 0 and 1 are scaled to be MIDI 0 to 127.
The " Cook  Every  Frame " option cooks the  CHOP  every frame, even if the  CHOP  isn't being displayed. All Volume Off and All Volume On flags are new and emit events for Controller 7 of all 16 channels. MIDI output go in a separate thread to allow output that slows TouchDesigner less. It now works in  Time Slice  mode for note events and controller events. (Not for Program Change or Sysex messages yet) Note channels only trigger anew Note On when the input channel goes from 0 or less to a value greater than zero. Similar for Note Off events.The channel name determines how it is interpreted.
For example,
ch3n60 - this channel is interpreted as channel3 note 60. A Note On event is sent when the value goes from 0 or less to greater than zero
ch5n - This channel will contain note numbers.¬† The value quantized to an integer, and when the integer value changes, the note of the old value goes off and the note of the new value goes on. If the channel steps from 53 to 78, it sends a Note Off event for note 53, and a Note On event for note 78.
ch14c7 - the value of the channel is sent to controller 7 (volume) of channel 14. By default, the values 0 to 1 are mapped to MIDI value 0 to 127.   These features work in  Time Slice  mode:
By default, channels are to start with "ch" followed by the channel number (1-16). In the case of notes, it is followed by "n" for notes, then digits for the note number. In the case of controllers, it is followed by "c" and a controller number. These prefixes can be altered. MIDI Out now interprets aftertouch, pressure, pitchwheel channels, and outputs these events to the MIDI stream. Note-normalization is added allowing 0 to 127 and 0 to 1 ranges. MIDI Out reads a bar ramp channel to output MIDI clock events¬† (with a channel popup menu to the parameter to select the channel name). Program change events are implemented through the "pc" channels.both 7 and 14 bit controller events can be output. You can capture a MIDI stream and output it to a file.   See also the  MIDI In DAT ,  MIDI Event DAT ,  MIDI In Map CHOP ,  MIDI In CHOP ,  midi  command.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: Enable or disable the MIDI Out  CHOP .

parameters.label: MIDI Destination
parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: ⊞  - Where the MIDI events are sent to. MIDI Mapper is the default destination.

parameters.label: Device Table
parameters.name: device
parameters.description: Path  to the MIDI device  Table DAT .

parameters.label: Device ID
parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Specify the id of which device to use.

parameters.label: One Based Index
parameters.name: onebased
parameters.description: Make the index 1 based instead of the default 0 based.

parameters.label: MIDI File
parameters.name: file
parameters.description: The filename of the output MIDI file.

parameters.label: Write MIDI File
parameters.name: writefile
parameters.description: Writes all the data to a MIDI file.

parameters.label: Channel Prefix
parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: The prefix string that all input channels must have in order to extract the channel number from their name (i.e. "ch1note44", with a channel prefix of "ch").

parameters.label: Cook  Every  Frame
parameters.name: cookalways
parameters.description: Forces a cook of the  CHOP  every frame. It should be On because the MIDI Out  CHOP  will otherwise only cook if the  CHOP  leads to a graphics display viewer. You want it to cooks whether you are displaying anything or not.

parameters.label: Automatic Note Off
parameters.name: autonoteoff
parameters.description: ⊞  - A MIDI 'All Note Off' event can be sent upon the start and/or end of the output.

parameters.label: All Notes Off
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: Sends an All Notes Off message to all MIDI channels.

parameters.label: All Volume Off
parameters.name: volumeoff
parameters.description: Sends an All Notes Off message to all MIDI channels.

parameters.label: All Volume On
parameters.name: volumeon
parameters.description: Sends an All Notes On message to all MIDI channels.

parameters.label: Send Start/Stop/Continue Events
parameters.name: startstop
parameters.description: Sends the appropriate events when the framebar starts or stops.

parameters.label: Send MIDI Timecode
parameters.name: sendmtc
parameters.description: While enabled, the MIDI Out  CHOP  will send MIDI Timecode (MTC) as a stream of quarter frame messages.

parameters.label: Timecode  Object / CHOP / DAT
parameters.name: timecodeop
parameters.description: The MIDI Timecode value to send. Should be a reference to either a  CHOP  with channels 'hour', 'second', 'minute', 'frame', a  DAT  with a timecode string in its first cell, or a  Timecode Class  object.

parameters.label: Note Name
parameters.name: notename
parameters.description: The base name of the note channels. If input channels have a number after the name, it is assumed to be the note number. If not, the channel value is assumed to contain the note number.

parameters.label: Aftertouch Name
parameters.name: aftername
parameters.description: The name of the aftertouch channel.

parameters.label: Pressure Name
parameters.name: pressname
parameters.description: The name of the channel pressure channel.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.name: notenorm
parameters.description: ⊞  - Values in the range 0-1 are mapped to MIDI value 0-127.

parameters.label: Pitch Wheel Name
parameters.name: pitchname
parameters.description: The name of the pitch wheel channel.

parameters.label: Controller Name
parameters.name: controlname
parameters.description: The base name of the controller channels.

parameters.label: Controller Format
parameters.name: controlformat
parameters.description: ⊞  - Sends 7 or 14 bit controller events.

parameters.label: 7 bit Controllers
parameters.name: 7bit
parameters.description: Send single 7-bit controller message.

parameters.label: 14 bit Controllers
parameters.name: 14bit
parameters.description: Pair two 7-bit controller messages to be interpreted as a single 14-bit message.

parameters.label: Note that the specified controller indices must be in the range 0
parameters.description: 31, since the range 32-63 is reserved for the corresponding message pairs to be sent. As a result, in this mode, the range 32-63 is reserved and not user accessible. Moreover, the range 64-95 is reserved for 7-bit messages, so any messages in the index range 64-95 will be sent as a single 7-bit message.

parameters.label: Normalize
parameters.name: controlnorm
parameters.description: ⊞  - Maps channel values from different ranges to 0-127.

parameters.label: -1 to 1
parameters.description: 1to1  -

parameters.label: Program Change
parameters.name: progname
parameters.description: The name of the program change channel.

parameters.label: Bar Ramp Name
parameters.name: barname
parameters.description: Clock ticks frequency is determined by the period of the ramp. The ramp must be 0 to 1. An incoming channel name for a 0 to 1 ramp over each 4-beat bar.

parameters.label: Ticks per Bar
parameters.name: barticks
parameters.description: Default is 96 = 4 beats * 24 ticks per beat.

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate
parameters.name: first
parameters.description: Use rate of first input to resample others.

parameters.label: Resample At Maximum Rate
parameters.name: max
parameters.description: Resample to the highest sample rate.

parameters.label: Resample At Minimum Rate
parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Resample to the lowest sample rate.

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ
parameters.name: err
parameters.description: Doesn't accept conflicting sample rates.

parameters.label: Export  Method
parameters.name: exportmethod
parameters.description: ⊞  - This will determine how to connect the  CHOP  channel to the parameter. Refer to the  Export  article for more information.

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Index
parameters.name: datindex
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the index of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name
parameters.name: datname
parameters.description: Uses the docked  DAT  table and references the channel via the name of the channel in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: Channel Name is  Path : Parameter

parameters.description: The channel is the full destination of where to export to, such has  geo1/transform1:tx .

parameters.label: Export   Root
parameters.name: autoexportroot
parameters.description: This path points to the root node where all of the paths that exporting by  Channel Name is  Path : Parameter   are relative to.

parameters.label: Export  Table
parameters.name: exporttable
parameters.description: The  DAT  used to hold the export information when using the  DAT  Table  Export  Methods (See above).

parameters.label: Rename from
parameters.name: commonrenamefrom
parameters.description: The channel pattern to rename. See  Pattern Matching .

parameters.label: Rename to
parameters.name: commonrenameto
parameters.description: The replacement pattern for the names. The default parameters do not rename the channels. See  Pattern Replacement .

parameters.label: Channel Names:  c[1
parameters.description: 10:2] ambient

parameters.description: 5] amb    This example fetches channels  c1 c3 c5 c7 c9  and  ambient .

parameters.label: start
parameters.description: Start of the  CHOP  interval in samples.

parameters.label: length
parameters.description: Number of samples in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: sample_rate
parameters.description: The samplerate of the channels in frames per second.

parameters.label: num_channels
parameters.description: Number of channels in the  CHOP .

parameters.label: time_slice
parameters.description: 1 if  CHOP  is  Time Slice  enabled, 0 otherwise.

parameters.label: export_sernum
parameters.description: A count of how often the export connections have been updated.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.

parameters.label: To re-compute the output data of the  Operators . An operator cooks when (1) its inputs change, (2) its  Parameters  change, (3) when the timeline moves forward in some cases, or (4)  Scripting  commands are run on the node. When the operator is a  Panel Component , it also cooks when a user interacts with it. When an operator cooks, it usually causes operators connected to its output to re-cook. When TouchDesigner draws the screen, it re-cooks all the
parameters.name: Dependencies
parameters.description: the necessary operators in all  Networks , contributing to a frame's total "cook time".

parameters.label: The term "Frame" is a measurement of time used (1) in the  Timeline , (2) as a time
parameters.description: unit in CHOPs, and (3) as a time unit in movie files that are read into  TOPs  and written out from TOPs. The frame rate is the frames per second ( FPS ).

parameters.label: The sub
parameters.description: Family  of  Component  types that are used to define and render 3D scenes. A  Geometry Component  is an Object that contains the 3D shapes to render. A  Camera COMP  and  Light COMP  are other Object types. Separately, "Objects" also refers to Python objects.

parameters.label: An  Operator Family  that manipulates text strings: multi
parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.label: TouchDesigner is a hierarchy of components. "root" is the top
parameters.description: most network in the hierarchy. The  Network Path  or Path for root is simply  / . A typical path is  /project1/moviein1 .
